sections.h2: What should a Mundelein owner know about selling?
sections.html:
Lake County is home to Mundelein, a village 33 miles from the Loop, and the recording for any sale goes through the county clerk's office in Waukegan. Owners generally compare an agent listing, a self-managed sale and a cash purchase of the house in its present state.

The village straddles Libertyville and Fremont townships and borders Grayslake, Ivanhoe, Diamond Lake, Libertyville, Hawthorn Woods and Vernon Hills. Its housing stock reflects its growth: ranches and tri-levels were built in the center of town in the 1950s and 1960s, and larger two-story houses followed on the edges from the 1970s.

That mix matters for pricing. A tri-level near the old center and a newer two-story near the village edge attract different buyers, and the repair needs are different too.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Mundelein?
sections.html:
Mundelein held 31,560 people in 2020, and the mid-2025 Census estimate of 32,680 is 3.5 percent above its base. Land area is 9.59 square miles, which works out to about 3,293 people per square mile.

Figures for 2020 to 2024 show a midpoint home value of $309,700, midpoint rent of $1,566 and midpoint household income of $108,340. Owners live in 71.2 percent of homes, spread over 11,632 households of 2.72 people, and a typical commute lasts 27.9 minutes.

  • At 2.72 people per household, buyers may look hard at bedroom count and basement space.
  • Hispanic or Latino residents make up 34.6 percent of the village, and 45.1 percent of residents age 5 and up use another language at home, so bilingual listing materials can reach more buyers.
  • Growth is steady, with the Census estimate above the 2020 count.

sections.h2: How did Mundelein grow, and why does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
The area was first settled by Europeans in 1835. The village went through several names: Mechanics Grove, Holcomb, Rockefeller and Area, before it adopted Mundelein in 1925 in honor of the Chicago cardinal. It was incorporated in 1909, after a spur line of the Chicago North Shore and Milwaukee Railroad reached the village.

The University of Saint Mary of the Lake opened in 1921 on the former Sheldon School estate, and in June 1926 the village hosted the closing events of the 28th International Eucharistic Congress. Ball Glass, a major employer, closed in the early 1980s, and the village added more than 10,000 residents between the 1980 and 1990 censuses.

A recent expansion is the 2022 annexation of more than 700 acres of land owned by the Wirtz family, where the plan was to build 1,200 houses and 600 townhomes. New construction near your house is competition to watch, so price against what buyers can find new as well as resale houses.

sections.h2: Which schools, roads and trains serve Mundelein?
sections.html:
Five elementary districts divide the village, so the one for your street varies. They are Diamond Lake School District 76, Fremont School District 79, Hawthorn Community Consolidated School District 73, Libertyville School District 70 and Mundelein Elementary School District 75. Mundelein High School serves the village, and Carmel High School and the University of Saint Mary of the Lake are private institutions in town.

  • Rail: Metra's North Central Service stops in Mundelein with weekday service between Antioch and Chicago Union Station. The station opened in 1996.
  • Bus: Pace Route 574 links Mundelein with Grayslake, Vernon Hills and other stops.
  • Streets: Lake Street, Illinois Route 60, Illinois Route 83, Maple Avenue, Midlothian Road and Hawley Street carry most traffic.
  • Interstate: Interstate 94 is five miles east.

The village hall opened in 2014 on a 10-acre site next to the Metra station, which puts the civic center and the train in the same place. Homes within walking distance of that area are easy to market on convenience.

sections.h2: Does Diamond Lake or the weather change how a Mundelein house sells?
sections.html:
Diamond Lake is a 153-acre glacial lake in south Mundelein, used for fishing, swimming and boating, and it drains to the Des Plaines River. Homes near it may appeal to buyers who want water access, and a lakefront or creekside lot should prompt you to confirm flood zone status before you list.

The village has a flood history. Floods in September 1936 and June 1937 damaged the main road and nearby businesses and neighborhoods. Disclose any water events at your own address on the seller report.

The Köppen label for Mundelein is humid continental, meaning warm to hot summers and cold winters. Since 1999 the extremes were 103 degrees in July 2012 and 26 below in January 2019. Swings that wide are why inspectors test the roof, furnace and sump pump.

sections.h2: What do Mundelein's building and permit offices require?
sections.html:
The Village of Mundelein posts a Permit Application for building and property work or new construction, plus a Homeowner Project Guide, and online fee payments. Contact customer service at 847-949-3283 or building@mundelein.org about a specific project. The main village line is 847-949-3200.

Gather permit records for any addition, deck, roof, furnace or finished basement before you list. An inspector will compare the house with that history, and a missing permit is simpler to fix before an offer than after one.

The village also provides water delivery and wastewater treatment, from a Lake Michigan supply. Ask the village about final water billing so the account closes at your sale date.

sections.h2: How is a deed recorded in Lake County, and are there extra transfer taxes?
sections.html:
Deeds are filed with the Recording Division of the Lake County Clerk, on the sixth floor at 18 N County Street in Waukegan (847-377-2575). Its published fees are $70 for a standard document and $82 for a non-standard one, and the only extra charges at recording are the state and county transfer taxes.

State tax under 35 ILCS 200/31-15 is fifty cents for every $500 of value. On the eRecording page the clerk names six municipalities whose deeds need local stamps or a signed exemption certificate: Buffalo Grove, Highland Park, Lake Forest, Lincolnshire, Mettawa and North Chicago. Mundelein does not appear. Most deeds qualify for eRecording, but a deed with a paper PTAX-203 cannot be submitted that way.

sections.h2: What should you prepare before accepting an offer in Mundelein?
sections.html:
The statutory disclosure report comes first: 765 ILCS 77/20 has the seller answer every item and deliver the report before a contract is signed.

After that, build the closing file with the parcel number, the latest tax bill, a loan payoff statement if applicable, permit records and the village water account details. Judge offers by the net amount and the number of contingencies, since a contingent deal can unravel late.

A cash purchaser may close within a short window and buy without repairs. A listing may bring more money but takes more time. Let your deadline choose.

faqs.q: Is there a Mundelein village transfer stamp?
faqs.a: The Lake County Clerk's list of six municipalities needing local stamps or an exemption certificate is Buffalo Grove, Highland Park, Lake Forest, Lincolnshire, Mettawa and North Chicago, and Mundelein is absent. The state tax of fifty cents per $500 still applies.

faqs.q: Which office takes a Mundelein deed for recording?
faqs.a: The Lake County Clerk's Recording Division, 18 N County Street, 6th Floor, Waukegan, in person or by eRecording through an approved vendor. Call 847-377-2575.

faqs.q: How much does Lake County charge to file a deed?
faqs.a: Its fee page gives $70 for a standard document and $82 for a non-standard one, with state and county transfer taxes as the only additions at recording.

faqs.q: Which elementary district covers my Mundelein street?
faqs.a: One of five: Diamond Lake 76, Fremont 79, Hawthorn CCSD 73, Libertyville 70 or Mundelein Elementary 75. Confirm by address, since Mundelein High School handles the older grades.

faqs.q: How do I start a building permit in Mundelein?
faqs.a: Use the Permit Application and Homeowner Project Guide posted by the Village, and call customer service at 847-949-3283 or email building@mundelein.org with questions.
